therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Adjusted mean change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 (LOCF)

results.effect_size: HbA1c change vs placebo: -0.69% (1 mg), -0.74% (2.5 mg), -0.84% (5 mg)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Reductions in fasting plasma glucose and 2-hour post-meal glucose consistent with urinary glucose excretion via SGLT2 inhibition
biomarker_changes: HbA1c reduced by -0.68% (1 mg), -0.72% (2.5 mg), -0.82% (5 mg) vs +0.02% placebo at Week 24
Fasting plasma glucose reduced by -11.0 mg/dL (1 mg), -21.6 mg/dL (2.5 mg), -28.5 mg/dL (5 mg) vs +4.1 mg/dL placebo
2-hour post-meal glucose reduced by -33.3 mg/dL (1 mg), -39.3 mg/dL (2.5 mg), -51.8 mg/dL (5 mg) vs +8.81 mg/dL placebo
Total body weight reduced by -2.69 kg (1 mg), -2.64 kg (2.5 mg), -2.69 kg (5 mg) vs -0.96 kg placebo
Systolic BP reduced by -3.7 mmHg (1 mg), -3.1 mmHg (2.5 mg), -4.6 mmHg (5 mg) vs +0.8 mmHg placebo
subgroup_findings: 53.6% of dapagliflozin 1 mg patients achieved HbA1c <7.0% vs 34.6% placebo (p=0.0157)
43.4% of dapagliflozin 2.5 mg patients achieved HbA1c <7.0% vs 34.6% placebo (p=0.2512)
49.1% of dapagliflozin 5 mg patients achieved HbA1c <7.0% vs 34.6% placebo (p=0.0726)
safety_signals: SAEs: 2 in dapagliflozin 1 mg (convulsion, tuberculosis), 2 in dapagliflozin 2.5 mg (uterine leiomyoma, pneumonia), 0 in 5 mg and placebo
AE suggestive of genital infection: 1 (1 mg), 5 (2.5 mg), 2 (5 mg) vs 2 placebo
AE suggestive of UTI: 3 (1 mg), 1 (2.5 mg), 2 (5 mg) vs 1 placebo
No major or minor hypoglycemic episodes in any arm
Hypotension AE: 1 patient in 5 mg arm
Creatinine elevation >=1.5x pre-treatment: 1 (1 mg), 1 (2.5 mg), 4 (5 mg) vs 2 placebo
Cardiac disorders AEs: 4 in 2.5 mg arm, 0 in others
